events.title: Samsung Galaxy Fold released
events.summary: Samsung began selling the Samsung Galaxy Fold — first mainstream foldable smartphone — 7.3-inch unfolded tablet phone.
events.about: Foldables forced Android developers to handle resizable and multi-window layouts on flexible displays. First mainstream foldable smartphone — 7.3-inch unfolded tablet phone.

narrative.whyChosen: The Samsung Galaxy Fold pushed foldable Android hardware into the mainstream.
narrative.whyImportant: Foldable form factors require adaptive UI patterns beyond fixed phone screens.
narrative.problemSolved: Phones were locked to a single rigid screen size and aspect ratio.

events.title: iPhone 11 released
events.summary: Apple released the iPhone 11 line on September 20, 2019 — dual cameras on the base model and Night mode computational photography.
events.about: Night mode and ultra-wide lenses made multi-camera assumptions standard even on non-Pro iPhones. Developers building AR and vision features could expect depth and wide-angle hardware on the mainstream model.

narrative.whyChosen: The iPhone 11 made multi-camera computational photography the default iOS baseline.
narrative.whyImportant: Night mode and ultra-wide sensors expanded what camera apps could assume on base iPhones.
narrative.problemSolved: Low-light mobile photography required third-party hacks or Pro-tier hardware.

events.title: .NET Core 3.0 and C# 8 released
events.summary: Microsoft shipped .NET Core 3.0 on September 23, 2019 with C# 8 — adding nullable reference types, async streams, ranges, and Windows desktop support.
events.about: C# 8's nullable annotations (`string?`) caught null bugs at compile time; `IAsyncEnumerable` enabled streaming async data; index/range syntax (`^1`, `..`) simplified slicing. .NET Core 3.0 also brought WPF and WinForms to .NET Core on Windows.

narrative.whyChosen: C# 8 nullable types changed how .NET teams handle null safety at scale.
narrative.whyImportant: Desktop support on Core let Windows apps migrate off .NET Framework.
narrative.problemSolved: NullReferenceException was the #1 .NET runtime bug; Framework-only desktop apps could not move to Core.

events.title: TensorFlow 2.0 released
events.summary: Google released TensorFlow 2.0 on September 30, 2019 — making Keras the default API and eager execution the default mode.
events.about: TensorFlow 2.0 dropped the 1.x graph/session model for imperative `tf.function` training — simpler notebooks and production pipelines. It unified the fragmented TF ecosystem and responded to PyTorch's research dominance with a more approachable developer experience.

narrative.whyChosen: TensorFlow 2.0 was Google's answer to usability complaints that drove researchers to PyTorch.
narrative.whyImportant: Keras integration and eager execution made TF competitive for interactive ML development.
narrative.problemSolved: TensorFlow 1.x's graph boilerplate was too complex for most practitioners.
